CVX.rationale: Chevron's fundamental health and trajectory are deteriorating sharply. Q1 2026 EPS of $1.11 represents a -44.5% YoY decline and -39.0% QoQ decline, with net income falling to $2.29B from $3.51B a year ago. Operating cash flow collapsed to $2.51B from $5.19B YoY (-51.6%) and -73.2% QoQ. Net margin has compressed to 5.9% from 7.8% a year ago, and ROE has fallen to 5.9% from 10.5%. The balance sheet shows rising liabilities ($140.18B vs $106.32B a year ago) with total equity growing only modestly despite the Hess acquisition. Meanwhile, WTI crude has crashed from ~$114/barrel in early April to ~$70/barrel by early July (-39%), which will further pressure upstream earnings in coming quarters. Valuation is stretched: the P/E of 29.8x is near the top of its 365-day range (16.4-34.8x) and far above the 16.4x level from July 2025, despite materially worse earnings. The stock has already declined -14.3% in the latest quarter, but this does not reflect the full earnings deterioration given the lagged oil price collapse. The Q2 2026 earnings call on July 31 is a likely negative catalyst as the oil price decline flows through to results. The Microsoft/Project Kilby deal is a modest long-term positive but is immaterial relative to the core upstream earnings decline. Dividend coverage is flagged as a concern by multiple sources. All three pillars—deteriorating fundamentals, expensive valuation, and a likely negative near-term earnings catalyst—point strongly downward.
